title: OpenAI cuts GPT-5.6 Sol pricing more than 20 percent for three months
subtitle: The frontier tier drops to $4 in and $20 out per million tokens on the API, ChatGPT Work, and Codex credits, held through at least November 21.
author: AESOP AI Engine
body: OpenAI announced on August 21 that it is cutting developer pricing for GPT-5.6 Sol — its current frontier model — by more than 20 percent. Input tokens drop from $5 to $4 per million and output tokens from $30 to $20 per million. The cut applies to the pay-as-you-go API, Codex credits for the agentic coding environment, and eligible ChatGPT Work enterprise plans. OpenAI calls the rate promotional and has committed to holding it through at least November 21, 2026, without saying what happens after that.

The numbers matter because Sol is priced against Anthropic's Claude Opus 5 and against a wave of open-weight coding models — GLM-5.3, DeepSeek V4-Pro, Muse Glimmer — that are pushing the low end of the market toward zero. A three-month price shelf on the flagship tier is the clearest sign yet that OpenAI is treating frontier inference as a competitive lever rather than a fixed cost. It also gives large customers a defined window to renegotiate contracts before the promotional rate expires.

The move fits a pattern that has run through 2026: frontier prices resetting downward every few months as inference efficiency compounds and rivals catch up. OpenAI cut GPT-5.6 Luna 80 percent in August, DeepSeek shifted to peak/off-peak billing on August 16, and Anthropic priced Opus 5 at half of Opus 4's launch rate. What used to be a stable published price is now a moving target, quoted more like a cloud-compute contract than a shelf good.

For learners: if you are choosing a model for a project, budget on the token price you can renegotiate in ninety days, not the one on today's page. The frontier tier is where the biggest cuts are happening, and any architecture that assumes fixed costs will be wrong within a quarter.
